cohort: 100 high-risk pregnant women undergoing caesarean section were included in the study (50 in each group).
finding: Carbetocin was found to be more effective than oxytocin in preventing postpartum hemorrhage, significantly reducing blood loss and the need for additional uterotonics with a comparable safety profile.
mod_finding: In women undergoing caesarean section, carbetocin was more effective than oxytocin in preventing PPH, reducing blood loss and the need for additional uterotonics.
